description: Stage 3, Gate 3c: build-process fixes (fast preflight, symbol-fact memory, a real progress readout) plus Phase 1 of the entity architecture - the shared cognitive workspace and the Continuity Law. No voice, no Person Model rollout, no Forge work in this gate.

userStories.title: Bake the network/token preflight into ralph.sh itself, aborting fast instead of burning iterations
userStories.description: ralph.sh currently starts iterating even when the model connection or GITHUB_TOKEN is dead, burning iterations on a wall it can't get past. Add a preflight check at the very top of ralph.sh, before the iteration loop: (1) a real one-token call to the configured --tool/--model (or the first model in MODEL_POOL if none given), (2) a real curl to https://api.github.com/user with GITHUB_TOKEN, both with short timeouts. If either fails, print the exact failing check and its raw output, then exit immediately with a non-zero code and ZERO iterations spent. Never silently retry into the main loop on a failed preflight.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: with GITHUB_TOKEN unset, running ralph.sh exits before any iteration starts, printing which check failed and why, exit code non-zero
AC2: with GITHUB_TOKEN set to a deliberately invalid value, the GitHub check fails the same way, real curl output shown, no iteration spent
AC3: with both checks passing (real model reachable, real token valid), ralph.sh proceeds into the normal iteration loop exactly as before, byte-for-byte unchanged behavior once past the preflight
AC4: the preflight itself never counts against --tool opencode N's iteration budget
userStories.verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && bash -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN= bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1; test $? -ne 0' && bash -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_invalidinvalidinvalidinvalidinvalid12 bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1; test $? -ne 0'
userStories.notes: Implemented in .ralph/ralph.sh only (no Kotlin, no app code touched). A preflight gate now runs after the arg parser and BEFORE the run log, the resume check and the iteration loop, so a wall costs zero iterations and leaves zero files: (1) real `curl -sS https://api.github.com/user` with -H Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN, 20s timeout, 3 attempts that fire ONLY when no HTTP status line came back (a real 401 is a verdict, used immediately, so a bad token still fails on the first request), then (2) a real one-token probe `opencode run -m "${MODEL_POOL[0]}" 'Reply with exactly one word: ok'`, 420s ceiling, rc!=0 / empty output / a match on the shared ROUTER_DOWN_PATTERN all count as failure. On failure each branch prints the exact failing check plus its verbatim raw output (the full curl body for a 401) and the script exits 1; there is no path from a failed check into the loop. Order is GitHub-FIRST (the story lists the model first): the token check is free and deterministic, so a dead token never pays a ~4-minute model probe, and both checks still run on a good-token run so AC3 is fully covered. AC1 proven on the stored verifyCommand's first clause: GITHUB_TOKEN= bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1 -> 'PREFLIGHT FAIL [github]: GITHUB_TOKEN is unset or empty.' + 'PREFLIGHT FAILED: aborting now, with zero iterations spent.' in 0.33s, exit 1, no run log created. AC2 proven on the second clause: a deliberately invalid token -> real request, HTTP 401, raw body {"message": "Bad credentials", "documentation_url": ..., "status": "401"} printed verbatim, exit 1 in 0.96s, zero iterations. AC3 proven two ways: (a) structural - diffing the region from `touch "$RUN_LOG"` to EOF against HEAD's gives only two hunks, the hoisted ROUTER_DOWN_PATTERN (value compared string-identical, now shared with the probe's provider matcher) and the PRD_FILE/GRADLE_PROPS/REJECT_HELPER assignments relocated above the gate; the iteration loop itself is byte-for-byte unchanged; (b) behavioural - a stub opencode (echo 'ok') + stub curl (200 /user) first on PATH with a real N=3 run executes 3 iteration banners, 3 full-prompt (~41k-char) tool calls and writes 'Iterations run: 3 of 3', i.e. the normal resume-check/loop/report path. AC3's real-network half proven separately with `bash .ralph/ralph.sh --preflight-only`: real token accepted (user: mhw77655-hue) and the real probe returned 'ok' in 3m50s, exit 0 without iterating. AC4 proven by that same stub N=3 run: exactly ONE short (31-char) probe call plus the 3 iteration calls, and the iteration budget reported was the full 3 - the preflight never touches MAX_ITERATIONS/ITER_REACHED and is not a full-prompt call. Added two escape hatches, both announced: --skip-preflight (deliberate bypass) and --preflight-only (run both real checks, print the verdict, exit 0/1). All four timeout/retry knobs are env-overridable (PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_TIMEOUT, PREFLIGHT_MODEL_TIMEOUT, PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_ATTEMPTS, PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_RETRY_SLEEP) and with_timeout() degrades to a bare call when `timeout` is absent. Stored verifyCommand run verbatim end-to-end: EXIT=0. bash -n clean.

userStories.title: Never pay a CI round trip twice for the same wrong-package guess
userStories.description: Ralph has imported the same class from the wrong package on two separate stories days apart (ModelProviderType: guessed com.jarvis.app.model, real location com.jarvis.app.env), each time only discovered after a full CI round trip failed on 'Unresolved reference'. Fix has two required parts, not one. (1) A new persistent fact file .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md, auto-injected into every Ralph prompt the same way REPO_FACTS.md already is. Any time an 'Unresolved reference' or 'cannot find symbol' compile error is diagnosed and fixed, the real class-to-package mapping gets appended here before continuing, in the form 'ClassName -> real.package.path (file:line)' - permanent, never re-discovered the hard way twice. (2) prompt.md gets an explicit, mandatory rule: before writing an import for any class not already in SYMBOL_FACTS.md or the file currently being edited, grep the real source tree for its actual declaration first (class/interface/enum class/object/data class) and use that real location - never guess a package by convention or by copying a neighboring import's shape.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md exists, is auto-injected into the Ralph prompt (same mechanism as REPO_FACTS.md, verifiable by grepping the injection code path)
AC2: a real test scenario - deliberately introduce a class the AI hasn't seen import for yet, confirm the resulting prompt contains a grep-first instruction, not permission to guess
AC3: prompt.md contains the explicit mandatory grep-before-import rule in its own section, not buried in unrelated prose
AC4: SYMBOL_FACTS.md already seeded with the ModelProviderType fact (com.jarvis.app.env.EnvironmentProfile.kt:254) as its first real entry, so this exact mistake cannot recur a third time
userStories.notes: Both required parts landed, plus a runnable end-to-end proof. (1) New persistent file .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md (append-only, 'ClassName -> real.package.path (rel/File.kt:line)' one fact per line, with the header documenting the rule and the format). Injection uses the SAME mechanism as REPO_FACTS.md but is now centralised: ralph.sh gained build_prompt() = cat REPO_FACTS.md / --- / cat SYMBOL_FACTS.md / --- / cat prompt.md, the loop calls COMBINED_PROMPT="$(build_prompt)", and a new ralph.sh --print-prompt flag prints exactly that composition and exits 0 (real prompt, no preflight, no iteration, no model call, no files touched) so prompt content is greppable offline. ralph.sh also re-creates SYMBOL_FACTS.md with a stub line if it is missing, so a fresh clone still runs. (2) prompt.md gained its own top-level section '## MANDATORY: grep the real source tree BEFORE you write any import', placed immediately after Phase 0 so it is read before any edit: (a) class already in SYMBOL_FACTS.md -> use that package; (b) class declared in the file being edited -> use that; (c) otherwise grep '^(data |sealed |enum |abstract |open )*(class|interface|object) <ClassName>\b' over mobile/app/src/{main,test}/java FIRST and import from the grep result, with the explicit note that a type nested in an object needs the full path (com.jarvis.app.threads.ThreadObjects.OpenThread), and an explicit ban on guessing by convention or by copying a neighbouring import's shape. It also states the append-back obligation: every fixed 'Unresolved reference'/'cannot find symbol' adds its mapping to SYMBOL_FACTS.md before work continues. AC1: file exists; the injection code path is greppable (SYMBOL_FACTS_FILE=\"$SCRIPT_DIR/SYMBOL_FACTS.md\" plus cat \"$SYMBOL_FACTS_FILE\" inside build_prompt) and a real `bash .ralph/ralph.sh --print-prompt` (48412 bytes pre-fact) contains the seeded fact verbatim. AC2: .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh is the real scenario, no network/model/gradle - it picks a REAL top-level class SYMBOL_FACTS.md does not know (alphabetically first unrecorded, or $1), greps its declaration, derives the package from that file's own 'package' line (never a guess), appends the fact, then prints the REAL prompt and asserts the fact AND the grep-first rule are both present. Deliberate-trap run: `bash .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh MemoryPolicy` -> com.jarvis.app.memory IS a real package, so 'import com.jarvis.app.memory.MemoryPolicy' looks obviously right and resolves nowhere; the grep found com.jarvis.app.env (EnvironmentProfile.kt:271), recorded it, and the rebuilt prompt carried both 'MemoryPolicy -> com.jarvis.app.env' and the prohibition ('Never guess a package by convention') - RESULT: PASS. The default (no-arg) run picked Accumulate -> com.jarvis.app.humancore.algo and also passed. --dry-run passes too (it skips the two write-dependent assertions and says so). AC3: the rule is a single '## MANDATORY: ...' heading (asserted to appear exactly once), contains the literal grep command, and sits between Phase 0 and '## Your Task', not inside unrelated prose. AC4: seeded, with the other two real burn-moment facts from this repo's history: ModelProviderType -> com.jarvis.app.env (EnvironmentProfile.kt:254, first entry), Cursor -> android.database (NOT the removed android.database.sqlite.Cursor), OpenThread/Completeness -> com.jarvis.app.threads.ThreadObjects (nested). Stored verifyCommand exits 0. Regression: RALPH-FAST-PREFLIGHT's verifyCommand still exits 0 after the ralph.sh edits, and a stubbed 1-iteration run proves the loop still ships the full composed prompt (1 short 31-char probe call + 1 49195-char full-prompt call, up from 41203 before injection). bash -n clean on both scripts. Files: .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md (new), .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh (new), .ralph/ralph.sh, .ralph/prompt.md, .ralph/REPO_FACTS.md, .ralph/progress.txt.

userStories.title: A real progress readout Venon can check without reading logs, reflecting only real story state
userStories.description: No honest, glanceable progress indicator exists today - only prd.json JSON and raw run logs. Build a small deterministic script (no AI call, no network) .ralph/progress.sh that reads the real current .ralph/prd.json and prints: a text progress bar sized to closed-count/total-count (e.g. '[####------] 4/10 stories'), each story's id and passes true/false, and if a .ralph/ralph_run_*.log run is currently in progress, the current iteration number out of its max. Must read the REAL prd.json passes field only - never a separate hand-maintained counter that could drift from real story state. Wire it to run automatically at the start and end of every ralph.sh invocation, printed to stdout, AND runnable standalone anytime by Venon.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: running bash .ralph/progress.sh directly prints a real bar matching the exact closed/total count read live from prd.json at that moment - proven by flipping one story's passes value by hand and re-running, the bar output changes accordingly with no other code touched
AC2: ralph.sh calls progress.sh once at start and once at end of every run, visible in a fresh run's own output

AC3: the bar never hardcodes a total story count - adding or removing a story in prd.json changes the denominator automatically on the next run, proven by a fixture prd.json with a different story count
AC4: no network call, no AI/model call anywhere in progress.sh - grep-provable, pure local file read and print
userStories.notes: New .ralph/progress.sh, plus the removal of the drifting counter it replaces. The script reads the ONLY source of truth there is - the live .ralph/prd.json - with jq: total = [.userStories[]?]|length, closed = select(.passes == true); it then prints '[####----------------] 2/5 stories closed - Friday (in progress)', one line per story with its real passes value and priority, and a run line. No second tally exists anywhere. DELETED the old print_progress_bar() from ralph.sh, which counted grep -c '"id":' against a hardcoded /sdcard path - a hand-kept proxy that drifts from the real passes fields, i.e. exactly the lying counter this story exists to remove. ralph.sh now has a one-line print_progress() wrapper and calls it three times: at the START of a run (before the 'Starting Ralph' banner), as --brief at the end of each iteration, and at the END of the run with --note carrying the run's real FINAL_STATUS and ITER_REACHED. AC1: ran the script, then flipped WORKSPACE-CORE's passes to true by hand in the real prd.json and re-ran with nothing else touched - the bar went 2/5 -> 3/5 ('[########------------] 3/5') and that story's line flipped to [x]; git checkout restored the file and the bar returned to 2/5. AC2: a fresh N=1 run of ralph.sh shows the readout in its own output at the start ('run: IN PROGRESS - iteration not recorded yet (runner pid 24911, up 6s)'), the brief line per iteration, and at the end ('run: this run finished - final status: max_iterations, iterations run: 1 of 1'). The model in that run was stubbed (stub opencode + stub curl, the established zero-token harness) so the loop control flow could be exercised without spending a real iteration; the readouts are produced by the real script from the real prd.json. AC3: no total is hardcoded - the same script against a 3-story fixture prd (1 closed) prints 1/3, and against a 1-story fixture prints 1/1 with a full bar and state 'complete'; the real prd still reads 2/5. AC4: pure local read+print (jq + file reads), no network client, no model call, no gradle, no writes; the stored verifyCommand's own '! grep -rnE HttpURLConnection|curl |fetch\(' clause passes, and an extra scan for wget/nc/ssh/opencode/api.github/http found nothing. Live-run detection is honest in both directions: ralph.sh writes its own pid to .ralph/.ralph_active after the preflight gate and removes it via trap on EXIT (added to .gitignore); progress.sh trusts the PID (kill -0) rather than the marker's age, because a legitimate multi-hour run would otherwise read as stale, and when no marker exists it falls back to a read-only /proc scan for a live 'bash ... ralph.sh' process so a run predating the marker still reports IN PROGRESS instead of claiming nothing is happening. Also added: --brief, --no-run, --note, an optional prd path argument, PROGRESS_BAR_WIDTH and PROGRESS_STALE_SECONDS env knobs, and explicit failure text when jq is missing or the prd is not valid JSON (state reported as UNKNOWN, never guessed). bash -n clean; both earlier stories' verifyCommands re-verified green after these ralph.sh edits.

userStories.title: The shared cognitive workspace: claims instead of named wires
userStories.description: This is the real fix for the isolation problem this project keeps re-catching in code review - no subsystem may read another by name. Add com.jarvis.app.cognition.workspace: a Claim (id, kind, payload, confidence 0..1, sourceOrgan, personId nullable - reserved now even though full multi-person scoping is a later gate, so this schema never needs a breaking migration for it, decayRate, createdAt, supersedes nullable) and a Workspace interface (publish(claim), claims(kind, personId=null), current(kind, personId=null) returning the highest-confidence live claim, decay/tick()). Existing hardcoded seams that already do this job informally (ContextWindowAssembler's deterministic union, the mental-state seam) get audited first and their real callers migrated to publish/read through Workspace instead of a direct reference - do not build a second, parallel state store alongside them. Any claim whose kind is tagged as a PREDICTION must carry a baseline field (what the naive most-common-answer would have been) and a wasCorrect nullable outcome field, set once the real next turn confirms or contradicts it - no predictive claim is allowed to exist in the schema without a way to later prove whether it beat guessing. Register as a real organ in JarvisOrganGraph with edges to whatever real callers get migrated to it.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: two different existing organs (audit finds the real two - candidates are ContextWindowAssembler's union and UserMentalStateEstimator's seam) are migrated to publish real claims through Workspace instead of their old direct-reference path, proven on the real TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine turn path, not a unit test in isolation

AC2: workspace.current(kind) returns the highest-confidence live claim among several conflicting claims of the same kind published in one turn - fixture has 3 competing interpretations of one utterance, the highest-confidence one wins, the other two remain queryable via claims(kind), not deleted
AC3: a claim's confidence measurably decays over simulated ticks per its decayRate, and a fresh claim of the same kind can overtake a decayed older one without either being deleted

AC4: a PREDICTION-kind claim's schema is asserted to require baseline and wasCorrect fields - constructing one without them fails to compile or fails a runtime schema check, whichever is real for the language
AC5: SystemGraphTest pins the new cognition.workspace organ and both migrated edges

AC6: full regression sweep stays green - the two migrated organs produce byte-identical real-turn output to their pre-migration behavior on the existing fixtures, proving this is a real substitution, not a behavior change
userStories.notes: New com.jarvis.app.cognition.workspace: Claim(id, kind, payload, confidence 0..1, sourceOrgan, personId?, decayRate, createdAt, supersedes?, baseline?, wasCorrect?), ClaimKind (the PREDICTION tag lives on the KIND, not the call site), the Workspace interface (publish / claims / current / tick) and the real InMemoryWorkspace - in-memory, synchronized, no storage target and no network call. personId is reserved now, so multi-person scoping never needs a breaking migration; a null personId on a QUERY means 'no filter', which is what makes both scoped and unscoped reads expressible today. Nothing is ever deleted: supersession and decay change only what current() answers, while claims() keeps every loser queryable. AC1: the two audited organs were migrated onto the store instead of a second store being built beside them. UserMentalStateEstimator now PUBLISHES each turn's MENTAL_STATE claim; ContextWindowAssembler no longer names the estimator AT ALL - its mentalStateEstimator constructor param and the CognitiveEngine line that fed it are deleted, and it reads the claim instead, publishing the assembled union as a CONTEXT_WINDOW claim. One shared instance is constructed at the single production composition point (JarvisEngine.init and its JVM twin TermuxJarvisServer) and handed to both. Proven on the real path, not in isolation: WorkspaceProductionWiringTest drives TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine.process (5 tests) and asserts the turn's MENTAL_STATE claim (sourceOrgan identity.mentalStateEstimator, createdAt a real instant, confidence = the vocabulary's own rule applied to that turn's reading) and the assembler's CONTEXT_WINDOW claim (payload carries the turn's segment turns), that turn 2 supersedes turn 1 without deleting it, and that a second composition's store starts empty (the store is wired, not a global). The claim text is a LOSSLESS encoding (MentalStateClaims.encode/decode over org.json, the pattern TurnTrace already uses in main code), so the hypothesis the window surfaces is equal to the one the estimator returned - proven by asserting result.assembledMentalState == MentalStateClaims.read(workspace) on the real engine. The continuity gate keeps its own snapshot contribution untouched, so no generation-payload byte moved. AC2: three competing INTERPRETATION claims for one utterance; current() returns the highest-confidence one and claims() still returns all three (asserted as the exact order c2, c3, c1). The order is total - confidence desc, then createdAt desc, then id - so equal-confidence claims always resolve the same way. AC3: confidence falls by the claim's own decayRate per elapsed Workspace.TICK_INTERVAL_MS (1s); a fresh stronger claim overtakes the decayed older one and both remain in claims(); a claim decayed to zero stops answering current() but is still retained. A late or duplicate tick is IGNORED and never rewinds the clock - WorkspaceCoreTest caught my first implementation doing exactly that (it set lastTickAt on an earlier instant, so the next real tick decayed twice as much); fixed in commit 2618e0e. AC4: in Kotlin the fields are non-null-typed, so the real enforcement is a schema check in Claim's init - a PREDICTION claim with a null baseline cannot be constructed at all, and InMemoryWorkspace.publish re-checks what it is handed. A non-prediction kind may not carry a baseline or an outcome, so a prediction cannot hide behind another kind. The outcome is set ONCE: re-publishing with a different wasCorrect throws, while settling it after the claim has decayed is allowed (the outcome belongs to the claim, not to its current confidence). AC5: SystemGraphTest pins cognition.workspace as a real COGNITIVE organ (com.jarvis.app.cognition.workspace.InMemoryWorkspace, not PLANNED), reachable from entry.latencyPipeline, with BOTH migrated edges - assembler READS_FROM the workspace and estimator SENDS_TO it - plus engine DEPENDS_ON it, and asserts the old assembler -> estimator edge is GONE. AC6: full sweep bash .ralph/ci_verify.sh '*' = 1288/1288 on run 36311887001 (1262 before this story, +26 new). Two corrections came out of verification rather than being designed in: 2618e0e (the tick clock) and 220a38a, where WorkspaceProductionWiringTest had asserted the FusionLayerTier1 reading ('pleasant', a measured confidence) on the TermuxJarvisServer path - that server wires the RULE-BASED default estimator, the emotion provider is folded in by JarvisEngine.init, so the real reading for that input is the unanchored neutral one. The migration itself was right; the assertion was not, so it now pins the real readings and the invariant that the published confidence is the reading's own anchored confidence when the emotion layer observed a signal and the declared UNANCHORED_CONFIDENCE prior (documented as 'a real reading exists but nothing anchored it') when it did not.

userStories.title: Layered change: fast state moves freely, slow state is rate-limited and logged, and a replay check catches drift
userStories.description: Depends on WORKSPACE-CORE. Add a ChangeLayer enum (FAST, SLOW, CORE) to claim kinds already known to be identity-adjacent (self-model, persona traits, person-model trust tier) - FAST is unrestricted, SLOW enforces a minimum real-time interval and evidence-count threshold before a change is accepted (not just proposed), CORE is rejected outright by this mechanism (those fields stay governed by the existing frozen-invariant path, untouched by this story). Every accepted SLOW-layer change is appended to a durable, queryable ChangeLog entry (what changed, from what to what, why - the evidence claim(s) that justified it, when). Add a ReplayCheck: given a small fixed set of real recorded turns (fixtures, not live conversation), replaying them after N simulated SLOW-layer changes must still produce responses a human-authored similarity check accepts as recognizably consistent with the pre-change baseline on at least the CORE identity facts (name, stated values, relationship to Venon) - a fixture-based regression, not a subjective judgment call left to the AI itself.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: a SLOW-layer change proposed with insufficient evidence-count is rejected, the same change proposed again after enough real accumulated evidence claims is accepted, both proven on the real path
AC2: every accepted SLOW change produces a ChangeLog entry with the old value, new value, justifying claim id(s), and timestamp - queryable, not just logged to text
AC3: a CORE-tagged field change is rejected by this mechanism unconditionally regardless of evidence count, proven by attempting one
AC4: the ReplayCheck fixture suite passes on a baseline run with zero simulated changes, and continues passing after a sequence of legitimate accepted SLOW changes

AC5: the ReplayCheck fixture suite FAILS on a deliberately-corrupted fixture (a simulated CORE-identity drift injected directly, bypassing the gate) - proving the check actually catches drift rather than trivially passing everything
AC6: SystemGraphTest pins the new node and its edge from cognition.workspace
userStories.notes: Layered change is enforced in one place. ChangeLayer (FAST/SLOW/CORE) is DERIVED from the claim's own kind + target field via ChangeLayer.forTarget, never declared by the caller, so a claim cannot vote itself FAST; a target the gate cannot classify is a construction-time IllegalArgumentException (Claim.init resolves the layer), and a non-identity-adjacent kind may not name a target at all. ClaimKind gained three identity-adjacent kinds (SELF_MODEL, PERSONA_TRAIT, TRUST_TIER) plus isIdentity; Claim gained `target` (16th field, named args at every construction site so nothing broke) and a derived `layer`. CORE = the real SelfIdentity fields (name, version) - rejected BEFORE anything is retained, always, and the pre-existing frozen-invariant path is untouched. SLOW = the real persona:<trait> facts PersonaTuner persists and the real relationship:<person>:trust tier: accepted only past BOTH a real evidence-count threshold (2 distinct real claims, one of which is this turn; re-proposing one claim id is a retry, not a second opinion) and a real elapsed-time interval (5s, read from the durable log, so it survives a process death). A rejected proposal is still RETAINED at EVIDENCE_CONFIDENCE 0.25 as evidence but never becomes the field's value - the ChangeLog is the only authority (ContinuityLaw.valueOf/historyOf/acceptedClaimOf read it, not an in-memory counter). AC1 proven on the real path: ContinuityLawProductionWiringTest drives the real TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine composition; one claim is refused, the second identical claim is accepted, and a second composition over the SAME data dir reads the accepted value back and then refuses an immediate rewrite because the interval came off the restored log. AC2: ChangeLogEntry(id, target, layer, oldValue, newValue, evidenceClaimIds, acceptedClaimId, timestamp) with the accepting claim provably one of its own evidence ids; FileChangeLog is the durable append-only JSONL implementation (entriesFor/latestValue/lastChangeAt/count, an unparseable line is DROPPED and the reader test pins count()==entries().size so a silent skip fails the suite); a NEW FileChangeLog over the same file reproduces every answer after a restart. AC3: a CORE claim is refused with zero retention in the store and zero log lines, and stays refused when the same CORE value is piled up 5 more times over 60s of real time; the version field is refused too. AC4: ReplayCheck re-renders the ONE committed fixture (mobile/app/src/main/resources/replay/recorded_turns.jsonl - 2 real turns, each carrying mandatory `provenance`, loaded from the app classpath so production, the JVM twin and the tests read the same copy) and is consistent on a zero-change baseline (fieldSimilarity 1.0) and still consistent after two legitimate accepted SLOW changes (persona:directness and relationship:Alice:trust), whose accepted values are then what the answer carries. The third check is RETENTION of the baseline's identity field names against a human-set floor (MIN_FIELD_SIMILARITY 0.5), not set similarity, because a legitimate accepted change ADDS a field. AC5 negative control: publishing a CORE claim straight into the production workspace (bypassing the law) makes the suite inconsistent, naming identity:name with expected JARVIS / actual HAL-9000, and every recorded turn reports it. AC6: SystemGraphTest pins cognition.continuityLaw as a REAL COGNITIVE organ (not PLANNED) with cognition.workspace SENDS_TO it and it DEPENDS_ON the shared workspace, reachable from entry.latencyPipeline. Both real composition points construct the law, the durable log (filesDir/identity/change_log.jsonl / <dataDir>/identity/change_log.jsonl) and the replay check; ReplayCheck is null-and-logged when a build packaged no recorded turns rather than defaulting to a fixture that passes everything. Disclosed limit: no live caller publishes an identity-adjacent claim yet, so the law does not gate a per-turn claim today - it is the acceptance path those claims must use, and ReplayCheck is what catches a change that bypasses it. MACHINE VERDICT (2026-09-28): stored verifyCommand EXIT=0 against CI run 36374009041 for HEAD 449efe9 (run conclusion success; remote main == HEAD so the run was reused, no push) - 53 matched testcases (ContinuityLawTest 11 + ContinuityLawProductionWiringTest 5 + SystemGraphTest 37), all passed. Full junit-results artifact of the same run: 1309 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped (1288 before this story, +21 new). Run 36365413999 had previously left 3 failures in 2 unrelated classes (OwnerBiometricBindingTest, PhaseBDisconnectedSubsystemWiringTest) caused by this story's own wiring test handing the process-wide HumanCore singleton a JUnit TemporaryFolder that was later deleted; fixed in 449efe9 by giving each composition a unique, non-deleted data dir.

userStories.title: Vision audit tool: check committed code against VISION.md Section 13
userStories.description: A script, .ralph/vision_audit.sh, run after any story closes. It reads .ralph/VISION.md and the diff/current state of the code a story touched. It checks that code against Section 13's checklist: closed enums or fixed taxonomies standing in for something that should stay open, thresholds that are bare constants where the vision requires them to develop with evidence, two organs calling each other directly instead of through the shared claim store, a class or file whose name claims permanent ownership of a cognitive function instead of declaring an affordance, and anything shaped like a resolver or arbiter making a meaning-level decision instead of a resource-level one. Use grep/AST-level detection for anything structurally checkable before spending a model call; reach for a model only for genuinely semantic judgments like whether a class name implies ownership. It produces two things every run: a report naming every finding with file and line, and, only for findings it is confident about, a real patch that runs against CI, sitting as a diff, never merged automatically. It never touches CONTINUITY-LAW-gated identity-adjacent state or the security floor. It never merges its own patch, never commits, never pushes, and never closes a story itself.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 positive control: run cold with no hints against the current repo and independently surface all three disclosed Section 12 deviations: ClaimKind's closed enum, ChangeLayer's fixed three-way classification, and the SLOW-layer's flat evidence-count-plus-fixed-interval threshold. Missing any one fails this story.
AC2 negative control: run against a legitimate construct that looks similar, the Workspace interface itself or InMemoryWorkspace's own internal fields, and confirm it is not flagged.
AC3 a real patch: for at least one of the three findings, produce an actual diff that resolves it and prove that diff passes the full CI suite on its own branch, unmerged.
AC4 no self-merge: prove structurally that no code path in the tool writes to main, commits, pushes, or closes a story on its own; only a human action does.
AC5 cost discipline: prove the structural findings are caught with zero model calls, and only the ownership-naming check spends one.
AC6 the tool audits itself: run it against its own source and report explicitly what was checked and why zero (or non-zero) findings is the honest answer, not silently assumed.

userStories.title: Bring VISION.md in line with Venon's stated vision: written record, seed, development, quarantine, floor layers, construction, closing law
userStories.description: VISION.md is the written record of Venon's vision. His latest explicit statement outranks it; where they differ the file is out of date and is revised to match him. Edit .ralph/VISION.md by replacing or inserting ONLY the passages below, using the exact wording given (plain ASCII), and change nothing else. Do not touch the headings or text of Section 4 or Section 13 (the audit tool parses them). Record every changed line range in notes. PASSAGE H replaces the title line and the first paragraph: title becomes '# FRIDAY - Vision (written record)', then: 'This file is the written record of Venon's vision of FRIDAY. Venon's latest explicit statement of his vision outranks this file: where he says something different, this file is out of date and is revised to match him - it is never used to overrule him. Everything else in the repo (plans, stories, code, audits) is subordinate to this file's current text and is read against it by every Ralph story and by the audit tool. This file changes only when Venon says it should.' PASSAGE P2 is inserted as a new paragraph after the first paragraph of Section 1: 'FRIDAY is a digital human: as close as possible to human personhood, individuality, development, relationship, understanding, emotion, values, agency and lived experience, while possessing machine-native capabilities that can exceed biological human limits - a human with outperformed machine algorithms. She is the person. Algorithms, models, memory implementations, tools, builders, external AIs and computational resources are what she has.' PASSAGE P3 replaces the Section 1 paragraph that begins 'This file is not a demand': 'The first FRIDAY is the seed of the final FRIDAY, not a small prototype of her. Her initial capabilities may be tiny; her developmental potential may not be. The seed already contains, in minimal form, the means of its own continuation: persistent identity, experience that can change her, observation of consequences, use of replaceable capabilities, recognition of capability gaps, a controlled path to acquire new capabilities, resource-adaptive computation, self-observation, and a protected continuity floor. The first FRIDAY has succeeded when she can keep increasing her own individuality and capabilities without Venon specifying her architecture or implementing each future capability by hand. Later capabilities described in this file are not demanded now; they are revisited as her development and available technology allow.' PASSAGE P4 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 3: 'Mechanisms are not the definition of development. The requirement is: experience -> persistent internal change -> changed later cognition or behavior, attributable to that experience, produced by mechanisms that stay replaceable, composable and extensible and that may grow beyond whatever we first invent. While her language model is a frozen organ, internal change means a change in what she decides or selects around it (how she reads a request, which capability or tier she uses, what she retrieves, what she has learned to do cheaply) - not a stored sentence replayed into a prompt. Every claim of development is tested by a Life Test on the real composition, with two controls: with replay of the original episode text blocked the change must still appear, and with the developmental mechanism disabled it must disappear.' PASSAGE P6 is inserted as a new paragraph in Section 5 immediately before the sentence 'Nothing outside this section may declare itself an exception to it.': 'Three layers are kept apart: the fixed floor (this section); bootstrap biases - the smallest set needed for her to begin functioning, each listed, justified and revisable only through the same ledger as any other change; and developed individuality - everything else, shaped by experience and relationship. We do not write her personality in advance.' PASSAGE P7 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 9: 'Construction capability belongs to the seed. From the first FRIDAY there is a controlled path: she recognizes a capability gap, describes the outcome she needs, requests construction resources, a candidate is produced and tested, it is approved (by Venon at first, later by her within the limits of Section 5), and it enters her capabilities. Ralph, GPT, Claude, search and other coding resources are tools she can call; they are not her.' PASSAGE P8 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 10: 'A milestone is closed only when it has all three: code with passing tests; automated Life Test evidence produced on the real composition; and something Venon can run and see or hear on his phone. A green report alone never closes a milestone.' PASSAGES B1-B3 are appended as three new bullets at the end of the list in Section 12: B1 '- The Human Core (four permanent passes, single-owner modules, rule-table learning, no part in her reasoning) is legacy scaffolding, quarantined: no new features, nothing new depends on it, and it is not her human side. Each part survives only while Life Tests show it contributes to her actual life without conflicting with this file; otherwise it is replaced or removed. Nothing remains because it was written first.' B2 '- Two compositions exist: the Android app wires the Human Core and the real resource snapshot; the JVM/Termux server stubs the Human Core and reports all-clear resources. Evidence from the second does not speak for the first.' B3 '- Intent is never classified (always STATEMENT), no prediction is ever formed on the live path, thresholds are flat, and the identity record still says JARVIS / he.'
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Passages H, P2, P3, P4, P6, P7, P8, B1, B2 and B3 are present in .ralph/VISION.md at the places stated, with the exact wording given.
AC2 No line inside Section 4 or Section 13 changed (git diff for this story shows zero changed lines in those sections); no other existing text was reworded.

AC4 Notes list every changed line range.

userStories.title: One Friday: one composition root for the whole turn path, shared by the Android app and the JVM/Termux server, with injected time
userStories.description: Today two entry points build two different Fridays. JarvisEngine wires the Human Core around the turn and the Android resource snapshot. TermuxJarvisServer builds its own graph, stubs HumanCore beginExchange/express/completeExchange to no-ops and uses an all-clear ResourceGovernor, so CI tests do not speak for the app on the phone. The turn path (cognitive, cognition, humancore, social, builder, failure) imports no android.* classes; the Android-bound files are in model/, latency/, memory/, identity/owner and JarvisEngine itself. Start with a Nano pass: use the SystemGraph to list every node that depends on JarvisEngine, TermuxJarvisServer and LatencyPipeline, plus the tests covering them, and put the list in notes. Then build ONE composition root that constructs the whole object graph from a small platform adapter (storage directory, resource-snapshot source, time source, speech and UI sinks, Android-bound stores). The Human Core is quarantined legacy scaffolding (VISION.md Section 12): wire it exactly as the app does today, add nothing to it. Network and cloud are resources around the same Friday, never a different Friday. All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Both entry points obtain their whole object graph from the same composition root and differ only through the platform adapter. A test builds both and fails if the set of constructed components differs by anything other than adapter-provided parts.

AC2 The JVM entry point no longer stubs the Human Core: beginExchange, express and completeExchange run on every turn there. A test shows Human Core state changing after a turn on the JVM composition.

AC3 Time: one injected time source is used wherever elapsed time changes behavior (decay, half-lives, thread resurfacing, session gaps, recency, mood); latency timers may keep the system clock. A test advances a fake clock by 72 hours and shows the effect on at least three time-dependent behaviors. Direct wall-clock reads that remain in the turn path are listed in an explicit allowlist test with a one-line reason each (for example latency timers); that test fails if a new unlisted read appears.

AC4 The Android entry point still builds (assembleDebug green in CI) and the full existing suite is green. Every existing test whose expectation changed because the stubs were removed is listed in notes with the reason; none is deleted to get green.
AC5 The platform adapter has two implementations (Android, JVM-test); adding another host later needs only a new adapter.

AC6 New runtime components are registered in the SystemGraph as the existing process requires (the graph is a map, not an authority). No new closed enum or fixed classification is introduced; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

userStories.title: Life Test harness: a scripted Venon drives the real composition and produces evidence packs
userStories.description: A Life Test is evidence about FRIDAY, not about code. Build a scenario runner that drives the unified composition from ONE-2-COMPOSITION through plain data scenarios and writes an evidence pack. Scenarios are data files in one folder so later stages add scenarios without touching the runner. Steps are data fields, not an enum: say(text), tap(target, outcome), wait(duration) on the injected time source, restart (tear the whole composition down and rebuild it from the same storage directory), night (invoke the idle opportunity if the composition offers one, otherwise no-op), assert over the recorded trace. The model is a scripted stand-in by default and a real backend by configuration, for the phone. Every scenario can also run in two control modes: replay-blocked (no original episode text may appear in any prompt or retrieval) and mechanism-off (the developmental mechanism under test is disabled). All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 The runner builds the composition through the composition root, never a private graph; each evidence pack records the composition's component fingerprint.

AC2 Scenario 0 'hello-restart': say hello; reply; restart with a DIFFERENT scripted model stand-in; ask her name and what was said; the trace shows identity persisted and the memory path used, so replacing the model organ left her the same. It passes on the unified composition with the Human Core live.
AC3 The runner can fail: a scenario with a deliberately false assertion is reported failed, and a test confirms it.

AC4 Scenario files accept an 'expect' field (pass or fail). A scenario marked expect=fail that fails is reported expected-fail and does not fail the suite; one that unexpectedly passes is reported unexpected-pass and does fail the suite.
AC5 Both control modes work: a toy mechanism that exists only in test code demonstrates that replay-blocked and mechanism-off each change the recorded trace in the expected direction.
AC6 The evidence pack (Markdown and JSON) lists each scenario with steps, trace excerpts, verdict and controls run. CI uploads it as a build artifact on every run of main.
AC7 Steps, scenarios and traces use open data fields: no new closed enum or fixed classification; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

userStories.title: Flight recorder and Development Ledger, both visible on the phone
userStories.description: The flight recorder says what happened. The Development Ledger says what FRIDAY became because of what happened. Neither prescribes what development looks like. Put a short schema note in notes. All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Flight recorder: every turn on the unified composition appends one structured record to a rolling local file: the input, what was considered and chosen at each decision point that exists today (intent, admission, tier served, context blocks included and their sources), request size, latency, degraded flag, reply, and any post-processing applied (Human Core openers, closers, guard actions). Fields are open key-value so new decision points add fields without a schema change. The app has an action 'Share last 200 turns' that exports at most 200 records.

AC2 Development Ledger: a durable append-only record. Each entry holds: what changed; which future behavior or cognition it can affect; the episode ids that caused or support it (resolvable in the recorder); strength of evidence; when formed and last reinforced; reversible or not and how; remaining uncertainty. Fields are open; no closed list of entry kinds.

AC3 No durable change to developmental state without a ledger entry: a test attempts a direct write to such state and it is refused. Ledger writes go through the existing continuity law and change log (extended, not a second competing store); the CORE refusal and ReplayCheck tests still pass.

AC4 Seeded ledger entries with provenance: the identity record, and exactly one bootstrap bias: 'Venon's explicit approval and disapproval are evidence of better and worse', with its justification and a note that it is revisable only through the ledger. No other motives, traits or values are seeded by this story.
AC5 The app has a Mirror screen that shows the seeded entries and any ledger entries, and when there are none says plainly 'Nothing has developed yet'.
AC6 Tests: the ledger survives a restart step in a Life Test; Scenario 0 leaves a recorder record per turn; the share action writes a file with at most 200 records.
AC7 No new closed enum or fixed classification; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

userStories.title: Final integration of the stage: full run on the unified composition and the Seed report
userStories.description: Final integration story. Run every scenario on the unified composition, regenerate the evidence pack, and write .ralph/SEED_REPORT.md answering the questions below. Label every answer FACT (with class or file, and test or trace evidence), INFERENCE, PROPOSAL or SPECULATION; where the honest answer is that something does not exist, say so plainly. Do not build new mechanisms in this story. Questions: Q1 What is the persistent entity? Q2 Where does her durable developmental state actually live? Q3 How can experience cause internal change? Q4 How does that change alter later computation? Q5 How are capabilities represented so they stay replaceable? Q6 How can the same FRIDAY use different computational resources? Q7 How can the seed identify a capability gap? Q8 How can it invoke the construction machinery? Q9 What is immutable? Q10 What can evolve? Q11 What remains from the Human Core, and what is only legacy scaffolding? Q12 What is the smallest Life Test proving the seed is developmental? Q13 For each Human Core part, does it alter or block behavior in any scenario in the pack (replies altered, vetoed)? Give a scaffolding verdict per part from the measurements. Q14 Does the existing capability-gap path (CapabilityGapDetector, ToolBuilder, DecisionEngine.missingCapabilities) connect to a live turn? Q15 What stands between today's repo and a seed that can acquire a capability with Venon's approval? All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 SEED_REPORT.md answers all fifteen questions, each labeled and evidenced, with no placeholder text.

AC2 Scenario DEV-1 exists as data with expect=fail and appears in the pack as expected-fail with the reason it fails. DEV-1: across several episodes Venon never states a rule but taps approve on bulleted replies and disapprove on paragraph replies to summary requests; the composition restarts; 72 simulated hours pass; a new summary request with different wording and different content arrives; the decision observed is the response format she chose, read from the trace, not from a stored value; run in replay-blocked mode and in mechanism-off mode as well.
AC3 The full suite is green, the APK builds, and the evidence pack is attached as a CI artifact; the report links to it.

AC4 Notes contain: exactly what changed; exact files and classes changed; what remains fixed versus newly developmental; the unified composition; the Life Test scenarios; the flight-recorder and ledger schema; full test results; any conflicts with VISION.md; every architectural assumption made.
AC5 Notes end with what Venon does next on the phone: install the APK from the last green run, send hello, open Mirror, use Share last 200 turns.
